question: A 27-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of recurrent episodes of headaches, palpitations, and sweating. He was adopted shortly after birth and does not know his biological parents. His pulse is 103/min and blood pressure is 160/105 mm Hg. Physical examination shows multiple soft, yellow papules on the tip of the tongue. There is a 2-cm, firm thyroid nodule. He has long and slender upper extremities, and his elbows and knees can be hyperextended. The most likely cause of this patient's condition is a mutation in which of the following genes?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Recurrent headaches, palpitations, sweating" -> "Symptoms suggest pheochromocytoma" -> "Thyroid nodule" -> "Possible medullary thyroid carcinoma" -> "Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B (MEN 2B)" -> "RET gene mutation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Multiple soft, yellow papules on tongue" -> "Mucosal neuromas" -> "Associated with MEN 2B" -> "RET gene mutation" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Long and slender upper extremities" -> "Marfanoid habitus" -> "Associated with MEN 2B" -> "RET gene mutation" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Hypertension and tachycardia" -> "Possible pheochromocytoma" -> "Part of MEN 2B syndrome" -> "RET gene mutation" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Firm thyroid nodule" -> "Possible medullary thyroid carcinoma" -> "Common in MEN 2B" -> "RET gene mutation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Hyperextensible joints" -> "Marfanoid habitus" -> "Possible connective tissue disorder" -> "FBN1 gene mutation" -> 60%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and physical findings are suggestive of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2B (MEN 2B). The recurrent episodes of headaches, palpitations, and sweating, along with hypertension, suggest pheochromocytoma. The thyroid nodule could indicate medullary thyroid carcinoma. The mucosal neuromas (soft, yellow papules on the tongue) and marfanoid habitus (long and slender extremities, hyperextensible joints) are characteristic of MEN 2B. MEN 2B is caused by mutations in the RET proto-oncogene.
